stories.title: Official says 273 arrested in NCCIA raid on 'illegal' call centre on Karachi's Sharea Faisal
summary: KARACHI: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Thursday claimed to have conducted a major operation against an alleged international fraud network and arrested 273 people from a call centre located on Sharea Faisal.
Last week, the agency claimed to have arrested over 40 suspects during a raid on an “illegal call centre” located on Sharea Faisal.
An NCCIA spokesperson alleged that the call centre was involved in fraud against foreigners.

summary: DC Raza directed the hospital administration to ensure the provision of “prompt, high-quality medical care” to all the injured.
A statement on social media said that the president extended his condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the early recovery of the injured in the accident.

CM Maryam “prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured passengers and extended her heartfelt sympathies and condolences to the bereaved families”, the statement said, adding that she sought a report on the accident.

stories.title: Comedian Russell Brand found guilty by UK court of rape and sexual assaults
summary: Comedian Russell Brand, once one of Britain’s most high-profile broadcasters and star of several Hollywood movies, faces a lengthy jail term after being convicted in a London court on Thursday of raping a woman and sexually assaulting three more.
Prosecutors said Brand, the former husband of US pop singer Katy Perry, was obsessed with sex and used women to satisfy his own desires.
One witness, a former friend with whom Brand later lived, told the court Brand had bragged that he wanted to sleep with 5,000 women.

stories.title: Gadi Eisenkot tipped to seek Israel government with backing of Arab lists
summary: Israel’s largest Arab list on Thursday said it would back Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government, bolstering his chances of being picked over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who lost the support of an allied religious party.

Ultra-Orthodox exemptions Meanwhile, United Torah Judaism, which backed Netanyahu after the previous five elections, in its meeting with Herzog declined to recommend Netanyahu again as prime minister, although it also did not side with Eisenkot.

The party informed Herzog “that it has decided not to recommend any member of Knesset to form a government”, the president’s office said in a statement, referring to the 120-member parliament in which United Torah Judaism has won seven seats.

stories.title: Largely peaceful marches take place across France as workers stage strike
summary: Some protesters clashed with police in Paris and Lyon on Thursday during largely peaceful nationwide demonstrations and a one-day strike by some public sector workers in a renewed challenge to President Emmanuel Macron.
French high school students and other demonstrators had earlier faced off against riot police in Paris as they blocked a street with rubbish bins on Thursday morning.
She estimated that some 250,000 people were demonstrating across France before the Paris march. “High school students, pensioners, students, workers, all together.

stories.title: Citizens in Islamabad left hanging amid unavailability of influenza vaccines
summary: A pharmacist running a drug store, wishing not to be named, said that the Chinese Sinovac, French Vaxigrip and American Influvac were the three primary flu vaccines available in the local market.

As prices have surged, due to shortages and transportation costs, they may not be allowed to sell at higher rates in Pakistan,” he said. “So I can say that the French vaccine Vaxigrip and American vaccine Influvac will not be available to consumers this year.
He also said that the flu vaccine was available in the market but some prominent brands were not available.

stories.title: Fresh polio case from KP’s Khyber district takes nationwide tally for 2026 to 9
summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan has reported its ninth polio case of the current year, with the latest infection confirmed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Khyber district, the National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC) said on Thursday.

The poliovirus detected in all three cases from Khyber district has genetic linkages to Afghanistan — which is facing an intense outbreak with 50 cases reported this year — indicating cross-border circulation of the virus,” it said.
On Sunday, Pakistan reported its eighth polio case of the ongoing year.

stories.title: Midterms over, Democrats plunge into wide-open 2028 presidential race
summary: Republican candidates will face a different challenge: how to distance themselves from Trump after Tuesday’s repudiation of his policies.

Scott Ferson, a Democratic strategist, said the party’s presidential primary could attract a huge number of candidates. “There are at least 30 Democrats who are saying to people close to them, ‘Do you think I should run?’” Ferson said.

Whoever emerges within the Republican Party as its new standard-bearer will face the task of keeping Trump’s ‘Make America Great Again’ (MAGA) base onside while rebuilding the broader coalition that powered his 2024 victory.

stories.title: AJK orders registration of all weapon licences within 10 days
summary: The Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) government on Thursday directed all holders of weapon licences residing in the region to register their licences at the nearest police stations within 10 days, warning that unregistered licences would be treated as cancelled.

Read: AJK police arrest 122 over attacks on law-enforcement personnel, property damage The unrest followed protests led by the Jammu and Kashmir Awami Action Committee (JAAC) over demands for constitutional and governance reforms.
In June, the AJK government declared the JAAC a proscribed organisation following escalating protests and clashes over the group's demands.

stories.title: CDF visits SSG headquarters, stresses operational readiness for tackling security threats: ISPR
summary: CDF Munir made the remarks during a visit to the Special Services Group (SSG) headquarters in Tarbela, where he was briefed on “specialised training, operational preparedness and mission-oriented readiness”, according to Inter Services Public Relations (ISPR).
He also witnessed a display of “state-of-the-art specialised equipment and a demonstration showcasing SSG’s combat proficiency, agility and precision in executing special operations”.
According to the statement, in his interaction with the officers and troops, CDF Munir lauded their “professionalism, high morale, and unwavering devotion to duty”.

stories.title: US warns of 'ongoing cyber threat' to industrial refrigeration systems
summary: The United States is warning of an "ongoing cyber threat" to industrial refrigeration ​systems, saying in a statement issued on Thursday that every organisation ‌that depends on cold storage should assume it could fall into the hackers' crosshairs.
Read: New cyberattack on supermarket fridges sweeps across Europe Malicious cyber actors are targeting industrial refrigeration & cold chain monitoring systems.
"Every organisation that depends on refrigeration ​and monitoring systems should assume it could be a target," said Chris Butera, CISA's acting executive ‌assistant director ⁠for cybersecurity.

stories.title: Nearly 600,000 demonstrate across France in biggest turnout of protest movement
summary: Nearly 600,000 people took part in demonstrations across France on Thursday, according to a provisional estimate by the Interior Ministry, marking the largest turnout since the protest movement began, BFMTV reported.

The General Confederation of Labour (CGT) trade union confederation claimed nearly 1.6 million protesters took part in demonstrations nationwide, compared with the Interior Ministry’s estimate of 600,000.
The Higher Education Ministry reported disruptions at 60 of 184 institutions, while the SNES-FSU union put strike participation among middle and high school staff at 52%.

stories.title: UNSC adopts Pakistan-initiated statement on 'role of diplomacy during active hostilities'
summary: The United Nations Security Council (UNSC) on Thursday adopted a presidential statement on the "role of diplomacy during active hostilities", an initiative spearheaded by Pakistan, the Foreign Office (FO) said.

The resolution, which was initiated by Pakistan, reaffirmed the UNSC's commitment to the peaceful settlement of disputes under Chapter VI of the UN Charter and underscores the importance of maintaining diplomatic engagement even after the outbreak of armed conflict.

The FO concluded by saying that the adoption reflected Pakistan's "continued commitment to multilateralism, dialogue and diplomacy", and its constructive contribution towards the maintenance of international peace and security.

stories.title: FCC bars PHC from hearing cases related to PTI workers' preventive detention
summary: The court order also directed KP Advocate General Sanaullah Khan to furnish a report to the top court within seven days in relation to the areas in KP where the armed forces were no longer required to act in aid of civil power.

The FCC said it may consider modifying the present order in terms of clause 4 of Article 245, which provides for calling in armed forces in aid of civil forces, after examining the report so furnished.

He cited clause 3 of the provision, arguing that a high court could not “directly entertain a case under Article 199 of the Constitution since it cannot exercise its jurisdiction in relation to any area in which the armed forces are acting in aid of the civil power”.

stories.title: Bank of England lifts rate for first time since 2023 to fight inflation
summary: The Bank of England (BoE) raised its benchmark interest rate to four per cent on Thursday, the first increase in more than three years, as soaring energy costs push up global inflation.
The central bank tightened borrowing costs by a quarter point, catching up with the US Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank in lifting rates since the start of the Middle East conflict.
The BoE on Thursday said its central forecast saw UK inflation peaking at 4.9pc in the second quarter of next year.

stories.title: From US Senate to Israel’s Knesset, Arab and Muslim electoral gains open paths to influence
summary: From the first Muslim elected to the US Senate to record gains for Arab-led parties in Israel, recent elections have opened new possibilities for communities long marginalised in national politics.

In Israel, political scientist Neve Gordon said anger over the war and other issues affecting Palestinians helped drive increased turnout, although he warned that racism and political exclusion could limit the influence of Arab lawmakers.
Zogby of the Arab American Institute said the election results reflected decades of growing political participation among Arab Americans, rather than a sudden shift driven solely by the Gaza war.

stories.title: Govt slashes petrol by Rs9.41, diesel by Rs5.56 for Nov 6
summary: The federal government on Thursday slashed the price of petrol by Rs9.41 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs5.56 per litre for November 6.
This marks the fourth consecutive day the government has reduced fuel prices, with petrol falling by Rs25.32 and diesel by Rs20.71 since Monday.
The latest revision also comes a day after the government slashed the price of petrol by Rs7.06 per litre and that of HSD by Rs3.71 per litre for November 5.

stories.title: Pakistan go down to India despite late onslaught in SAFF Championship opener
summary: Pakistan scored twice in stoppage time, including a spectacular overhead kick by Alamgir Ghazi, but their late rally proved insufficient as Nolberto Solano’s side suffered a 3-2 defeat against India in their SAFF Championship opener at the National Stadium in Dhaka on Thursday.
Trailing 3-0 at half-time, Pakistan mounted a spirited fightback, with Najeebullah and Alamgir finding the net in injury time to give the Shaheens hope of an unlikely comeback.
Najeebullah reduced the deficit in the second minute of stoppage time, powering home a bullet header from a Junaid Shah cross to score his first international goal.

stories.title: PTI workers detained in UAE: LHC terms foreign ministry's report unsatisfactory
summary: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Thursday termed a report submitted by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs regarding the detention of two PTI-affiliated Pakistani citizens in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) unsatisfactory and summoned the relevant official at the next hearing.

On Sept 14, the LHC had directed the foreign secretary to process and decide within 15 days representations concerning the detention of two citizens — Syed Salman Raza Zaidi and Muhammad Junaid Jahangir.

In a reply submitted through the attorney general’s office on Thursday against the contempt pleas, the ministry said it referred the matter to the mission immediately after receiving the court’s directions.

stories.title: 11 killed, 33 injured as bus collides with truck near Punjab's Pakpattan
summary: At least 11 people, including a Patrolling Police official and a Para Force personnel, were killed and 33 others injured on Thursday when a passenger bus collided with a truck on Depalpur Road, a Rescue 1122 spokesperson, Umair Iqbal, said.

Read: 464 die in Punjab road crashes in October Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz sought a report on the accident and directed the district administration to ensure the provision of the best possible medical facilities to the injured.
In October alone, 44,797 road traffic accidents were reported across Punjab, leaving at least 464 people dead and 23,543 seriously injured, according to Rescue 1122.

stories.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces international retirement
summary: Cristiano Ronaldo said on Thursday he was retiring from the Portugal team, bringing the curtain down on one of the most illustrious international careers in the history of football.

Portugal, who top Nations League Group A4, host second-placed Denmark on November 14 in Braga before visiting Wales in their final two group games, which will be Ronaldo’s final chances to add to his international statistics.

Ronaldo will leave the international stage as Portugal’s most successful player in terms of individual and team honours and has become a cultural reference point for the country around the world. “I spent my life working to become the best player in the world.

stories.title: Army foils TTP infiltration attempt in Kurram, retaliates to 'unprovoked' Afghan firing: state media
summary: The latest escalation followed an incident on November 1 when security forces responded to unprovoked firing from Afghan border posts near Angoor Adda in South Waziristan, forcing Afghan Taliban personnel to abandon their positions.

In another incident on October 30, the Pakistan Army successfully targeted and destroyed several posts and military positions of the Afghan Taliban in the areas adjacent to South Waziristan and Parachinar.
On October 27, Afghan Taliban forces opened fire on Pakistani border posts and civilian areas in Angoor Adda, Lower South Waziristan.

stories.title: IMF country head urges Pakistan to broaden tax base, pursue growth-oriented reforms
summary: He said Pakistan had reached a critical juncture where the narrative needed to change, with discussions moving beyond taxation to focus on how reforms could translate into investment, economic activity, exports, employment and improved living standards.

Binici outlined five key areas that could help improve the country's growth prospects, including preserving macroeconomic stability and strengthening the foundations needed to transform the economy from stabilisation to sustainable growth.

The IMF has repeatedly raised concerns over Pakistan’s taxation system and the slow implementation of structural reforms, particularly those aimed at improving the governance of state-owned enterprises, reducing market interventions and enhancing transparency in public finances.

stories.title: Trump faces new political reality as Democrats vow investigations
summary: President Donald Trump was left to grapple on Thursday with the stinging rebuke from voters after a midterm election rout, while triumphant Democrats vowed to lower prices and combat the “cartel” within the White House in the new Congress.
It will be the first time that Trump, a Republican who also held the White House from 2017 to 2021, has had to contend with a Democratic-controlled Congress in both chambers.

Trump had cast the midterm elections as a referendum on the first half of his second four-year stint in the White House, repeatedly urging his Republican base to “pretend I’m on the ballot”, a message that Democratic Party leaders were happy to amplify.

stories.title: Netanyahu's position weakens as rival secures broad backing to try to form government
summary: Benjamin Netanyahu's position ​in the post-election battle to stay on as Israel's prime minister weakened on Thursday after an ultra-Orthodox Jewish party withheld support for ‌any nominee and two Arab-led parties endorsed his main opponent.

Israel's president Isaac Herzog was due to meet Netanyahu and his chief political rival Gadi Eisenkot to decide which of the two men to pick to form a government, after holding talks with smaller parties.

And while Eisenkot, like Netanyahu, has so far ruled out forming a government with Israel's two Arab-led parties, both factions endorsed Eisenkot on Thursday, giving him backing ​from a comfortable majority of lawmakers.

stories.title: Lahore’s air pollution a year-round problem, worsened by winter and agricultural burning: report
summary: On Monday, air pollution in Lahore reached hazardous levels, with the Air Quality Index (AQI) crossing 530 and fine particulate matter (PM2.5) concentrations climbing to 343 micrograms per cubic metre.

Citing the Urban Unit’s 2023 Lahore emissions inventory, which was based on 2020–21 data, the report said that transport accounted for about 35pc of the city’s PM2.5 emissions, compared with 33pc from crop-residue burning, 29pc from waste burning and three per cent from industry.

Alongside monitoring infrastructure, the Punjab government has been implementing a multi-sectoral air pollution reduction strategy targeting transport, industrial emissions, brick kilns and agricultural burning.

stories.title: CDF Munir emphasises indigenous defence capabilities, sustained training to maintain security edge
summary: During the visit, CDF Munir was briefed on the SSG's specialised training regime and operational capabilities.

Read: Pakistan tests indigenous Fa'az missile “He also witnessed a display of state-of-the-art specialised equipment and a demonstration showcasing SSG’s combat proficiency, agility and precision in executing special operations,” the ISPR said.
The developments reflect the military's stated focus on combining specialised training, technological advancement and indigenous defence capabilities to address changing operational requirements.

stories.title: US' Rubio on 'resignation watch' following midterm defeat as he weighs presidential bid: report
summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is on "resignation watch" following Republican losses in the midterm elections as allies anticipate an exit to prepare a 2028 presidential run, Britain's The Independent reported.

"It makes complete sense for him to step down and leave the administration," a Rubio ally told the outlet, arguing that the top diplomat cannot run an effective nationwide campaign while serving in office.

Insiders said Rubio also seeks to separate his political brand from the Iran war to leave ownership of the war to US President Donald Trump, pointing out that he maintained a "quieter role" on military operations despite holding statutory foreign policy authority.

stories.title: PM directs cancellation of petrol pump licences over failure to facilitate fuel subsidy beneficiaries
summary: The meeting was informed that 15,519,282 citizens had registered under the subsidy scheme so far, including 15.06 million motorcycle owners and 449,000 owners of vehicles with engine capacities of up to 800cc.
PM Shehbaz announced a relief scheme in September for owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles with engine capacities of up to 800cc.

Under the scheme, owners of two- and three-wheeled vehicles are eligible for a subsidy of Rs100 per litre on a monthly quota of 20 litres, while owners of vehicles with engine capacities of up to 800cc are entitled to the same subsidy on a monthly quota of 30 litres.

stories.title: Minister says electoral reforms panel to have 2 members each from PML-N, PPP and PTI
summary: The ruling PML-N, its coalition partner PPP and the opposition PTI will each get two seats on the proposed Parliamentary Committee on Electoral Reforms (PCER), Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said on Thursday.
He said the opposition leader should nominate representatives to the committee on electoral reforms and submit the names to the Speaker’s Office.

During the meeting, the PPP delegation invited the opposition to participate in the parliamentary committee to promote consultation and discussion among parliamentary representatives on electoral reforms.

stories.title: New wave of bomb threats hits passenger flights across Europe
summary: Airlines across Europe received a series of bomb threats on Thursday morning for the second time this week, forcing many to make unplanned or escorted landings, although none of the threats immediately proved to be genuine.
Bulgarian officials reported three aircraft making emergency landings in the Balkan country because of bomb threats.
On Tuesday, at least seven flights and a cruise ship received bomb threats, causing disruption at airports across Europe, although no devices were discovered.

stories.title: Abdul El-Sayed backs Trump’s call to cut Israel aid, says he is willing to work with president
summary: Abdul El-Sayed, the first Muslim American elected to the US Senate, voiced support on Thursday for President Donald Trump’s remarks about cutting aid to Israel, saying Washington should stop financing a military accused of committing atrocities with American weapons.
El-Sayed told MS NOW that he agreed with Trump’s position and was willing to work with the president to end US military assistance to Israel. “I agree with him on that.
El-Sayed, who was elected on Tuesday, stressed the need to distinguish Judaism and Jewish people from the actions of Israel, and rejected attempts to portray criticism of Israel as hatred of Jews.

stories.title: 'What intrigued me the most was that it was a true story': Talha Chahour on 'Rutba'
summary: However, Chahour was careful to distinguish between the real individuals and their fictional portrayals. “It is better that we don't talk about the real people, but if we can discuss the character, it is not just about his story as an ASP,” he explained.

Rather than portraying Hadi as someone who always makes the right decisions, the drama allows audiences to see his vulnerabilities and mistakes. “Hadi's journey will show a real human being who stumbles,” Chahour said.
For Chahour, an actor's appearance should reflect the requirements of a role rather than simply prioritising looking attractive on screen. “I don't work to look good, but to look real,” he said.

stories.title: ECP sets Feb 7 as polling date for first phase of Punjab local govt elections; KP polls delayed
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Thursday decided to hold the first phase of local government elections in Punjab on Feb 7, 2027, in view of fog and weather conditions, while polls in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa were postponed until further orders.
It was further decided that the first phase of local government elections in Punjab will be held with the polling date set as Feb 7, 2027.
After deliberation, it was decided that in view of the said order, holding local government elections in the remaining districts of KP was no longer possible.

stories.title: Federal government announces Nov 9 public holiday for Iqbal Day
summary: The Punjab government also declared November 9 a public holiday in the province to mark the 149th birth anniversary of Iqbal, the national poet of Pakistan.
The Sindh government on Wednesday announced that all public and private schools across the province would remain closed on November 9 to observe the occasion.
Born on November 9, 1877, in Sialkot, Allama Muhammad Iqbal was a prominent poet and philosopher of the subcontinent who played a significant role in the Pakistan movement.

stories.title: Democrats to investigate Trump deals, with eye on 2028 race
summary: After sweeping both chambers of the US Congress, Democrats will turn their new investigative powers on the Trump family's business deals as they make what they call corruption a central part of a 2028 campaign for the White House.
Democrats seized control of ​both the Senate and the House of Representatives in Tuesday's midterm elections, in which tens of millions of voters delivered a rebuke to President Donald Trump.
Democrats have opted for investigations rather than trying to impeach Trump immediately, Reuters previously reported.

stories.title: NCCIA arrests 273 people, including 42 minors, in Karachi call centre raid
summary: Court grants NCCIA two-day remand of nine suspects in the case Earlier today, a judicial magistrate granted the NCCIA a two-day physical remand of nine key suspects arrested during the raid.

The investigating officer told the court that 273 suspects had been arrested during the operation and were being detained at the call centre premises, which the Home Department had declared a sub-jail through a notification.
Call centre raid At around 8-9pm, the NCCIA raided a call centre, Voxtron, located in PECHS near Shahrah-e-Faisal in Karachi on November 3, eyewitnesses told The Express Tribune.

stories.title: One dead, two injured after shop roof collapses on Karachi’s Manghopir Road: rescue services
summary: KARACHI: One person was killed and two others were injured after the roof of a corner shop collapsed near the New Nazimabad Flyover in Karachi on Thursday, rescue services said.
Rescue 1122 recovered three individuals from the debris, who were taken to a hospital.
On Oct 27, one person was killed, while seven others were injured, when the roof of an under-construction building collapsed near Multan’s Northern Bypass.
